title: Dedollarisation in Asia Will Build From the Bottom Up
text:
Asia-Pacific Macro Note | November 2026
Summary: The US dollar still dominates Asian trade and finance. Yet a shift in its international role has begun at the base of the system. In this note, bottom-up describes the order of change, not who drives it. Payments and local currency settlement are moving first, largely led by central banks. Trade invoicing will follow slowly. Reserves and funding will move last. Over the next 10 to 15 years, this points to deeper local currency markets and a larger regional role for currencies in active settlement corridors. It does not point to the end of the dollar.

title: Yong Jie Tan
text:
I am an economist currently pursuing a Master of Commerce in Economics at the University of Auckland. Previously, I served as a Research Associate at the Tun Ismail Ali Center of Excellence (TIACOE) at the Asia School of Business, in collaboration with MIT Sloan.

Research Interests & Ideas
My work operates at the intersection of macroeconomics, monetary systems, and industrial organization. I am actively researching:

Platform Economics: How digital platforms utilize native tokens to solve coordination problems in two-sided markets, and the role of internet information gatekeepers.
Monetary Systems: The transition toward retail fast payment systems (FPS), Central Bank Digital Currencies (CBDCs), and regional dedollarization.
Central Bank Communication: Leveraging Natural Language Processing and Large Language Models to measure policy alignment in central banking speeches.



Beyond Economics
When I am not working on structural estimation models, I am usually training for my next long-distance marathon, on the badminton court, or pulling times on the rowing ergometer.
